en.html:
Knives, chopping boards, pots. Rice, miso, dried horse mackerel. I was fairly sure these had been available five hundred years ago also.

I did not contribute this information. I nodded.

Indeed, without some explanation of that sort, it was difficult to understand how breakfast had resulted in half a kitchen.

en.html:
Muramasa"...Such nice weather, na."
Kageaki"If winter maintained this standard, I would have no serious objection to it."
Muramasa"You don't like the cold?"
Kageaki"I have the normal human objection, yes."
Kageaki"Heat troubles me more, though..."
Muramasa"For me it was cold, I think. Now I am a tsurugi, so neither is a problem."
Kageaki"As the saying goes, in winter you can put on more clothes and heat the room. Summer does not become bearable even after you have removed everything. In your time, did nobody make this observation?"
Muramasa"No... but I understand the point."
Muramasa"Only, listen..."
Kageaki"Hm?"
Muramasa"Every time you feel cold, you keep burning fuel, and the expense, uff. It really adds up. In winter you had to decide: warm yourself and accept less food, or eat and stay cold."
Muramasa"So winter has not left me such happy memories."
Kageaki"Ah... I see."

Muramasa"Summer heat, at least, you cannot do anything about. From the beginning itself you can say chhodo and give up."
Kageaki"You have arrived at the argument from the opposite direction."
Muramasa"Well... still..."
Kageaki"Yes."
Muramasa"Spring and autumn are better than both, obviously."
Kageaki"On that point, complete agreement."
Muramasa"Somewhere across the sea there are countries where spring goes on all year, no?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Muramasa"If we could live there... how nice that would be."
Kageaki"Yes. Though a little... lonely also, perhaps."
Muramasa"...Achha. No watching the four seasons change. That pleasure would go."
Kageaki"Summer nights, winter scenery. Complain as I may, I would be sorry to lose them."
Muramasa"Then learning to accept things is the main matter? Otherwise we start asking for luxury and the demands will never finish."
Kageaki"Who can say? Perhaps science will advance until we can choose whichever season we like."
Kageaki"Then make any demand. All shall be satisfied. Human wisdom will have achieved victory."
Muramasa"Yes."
Kageaki"Indeed."
Muramasa"..."
Kageaki"..."
Muramasa"One minute. Are we actually losing and calling it our victory?"

en.html:
What were we talking about? Nothing of importance.

Not moving our mouths because there was something to say. Finding something to say because the mouths wanted to keep moving.

And walking like that.

Going nowhere in particular.

No purpose was being served by this time. Worthless, though, I did not consider it.

Let it continue like this. That was what I wanted.
